means: Where the whole is weakest right now, read from every project's data, to choose the next piece of work.
not: Whatever is loudest.

means: One landed piece of work: a branch, one squash commit on main, and its record.
not: changeset (a bundle in Knope, one file in changesets - two meanings); commit (git's unit; a change may take many)

means: An idea a project rests on, with why it matters.
not: What a word means: that is the vocabulary.

means: A place for a family of stars: they work independently, benefit from each other and share a purpose - they belong together. It gathers its stars' data and keeps its own: what holds between its stars, and what is decided for them together. A star may belong to several.
not: observatory (looking, not belonging); organization (GitHub's word); the earlier use of lens for a group of projects

means: A shared process that carries work from one state to the next - built, tested, delivered - which projects call, not copy.
not: A template to copy.

means: Chosen by the observatory's keepers to stand in its navigation. Any lens can still be found without it.
not: Approved or owned.

means: An owned fork of someone else's code (Rhizoid's rhizcut): pinned to an exact upstream point, changed only as named patches each written to go home.
not: A divergent copy.

means: A choice taken, with why, and with what was rejected.
not: A plan or a wish.

means: Minutes weighted by how draining they were (load 0-10, Borg CR10): five counts as one. A short heavy chore can outweigh a long light one.
not: Time alone.

means: A project's whole chain on one page: why it exists, what it must reach, how each step is delivered and proven, what is happening now.
not: A summary.

means: The outermost lens: the one made of all the others, showing how they connect - what the world calls a board, taken to its full potential. One continuous sky with the story behind it, its relations, its history and its intent, and no walls. Every place has the same fulldome, over whatever that place holds: a star's own data, a constellation's stars' data and its own, an observatory's constellations'.
not: board (one lens: the flow of work); room, wall; a lens beside the others (it holds them); a show to sit through

means: A small daily job in each project that writes down what its work produced: commits, releases, test runs.
not: A person keeping records.

means: One look at work just done, recorded while fresh through ocoeco: what was done, what it advances, what it touched, and the effort - most of it filled in from what ocoeco already knows.
not: snapshot (filesystem and VM snapshots), exposure (risk), frame (software), observation (what the observatory as a whole does), entry (says nothing)

means: The observatory's reading of every marked project's tables, every few hours.
not: A copy of the projects.

means: One of the three stretches of a path: working (it does its job), perfection (as good as it should be), ongoing perfection (it stays so).
not: A deadline.

means: Why a project exists, written by the project itself for someone who knows nothing about it.
not: A feature list, or a summary for insiders.

means: A way of seeing, and the concrete mechanism for it: the data it needs, where that data comes from, and how it is shown - a structure of Markdown files, HTML and CSS, a terminal, anything. It must say the data it needs and one way to show it; bringing its own instruments for producing that data is optional. A lens is made once and used by anyone in ocoeco, in their star or constellation: the data and its structure are known, so it just works. A lens may be made of lenses.
not: view (SQL's word for one query); dashboard, report; plugin (it adds no code path of its own to a star)

means: How draining an action was this time, from 0 (nothing) through 5 (hard) to 10 (maximal), after Borg's CR10 scale of perceived exertion.
not: How long it took: that is minutes.

means: An action done by hand that a tool could do: counted with its minutes and load, and when it was done, until something automates it.
not: Bad work: it is a measure of where a tool would help, not a judgment.

means: The small file (oco.toml) by which a repository says: I am part of the commons, and here are my tables.
not: A badge someone else gives.

means: A step on a path, reached only when its evidence exists.
not: A date or a promise.

means: A place for someone's looking: it gathers the constellations, stars and other observatories its owner cares to see. They do not belong to it and need not know of it. Anyone can have one.
not: constellation (belonging, not looking); the one observatory (there are many); OCO (the ecosystem)

means: The part of ocoeco that observes: it finds places by their marks and gathers what they keep - the same act whether a constellation gathers its stars or an observatory gathers constellations and other observatories. It brings the data and the names of the lenses; a render already made may be taken as it is.
not: observatory (a place; the observer is an act of ocoeco); harvest, discover (its earlier names: a farm's word and a search's)

means: The ecosystem that lets anyone keep stars, show constellations and have an observatory: the agreement and its tools - ocoeco, tad, oco-agent, the lens tool. Not an observatory itself.
not: the author's observatory (one of many, made with OCO); open commons (the principle, wider than OCO)

means: The commons' language and machinery: the tables, the mark, the gatherers and the checks - the blood and heart every project lives by.
not: The observatory's website.

means: What a project must reach: its milestones on three horizons, each with the evidence that proves it.
not: A plan of dates.

means: A repository with a mark. It keeps its own idea, path, workings and work, in its own data.
not: A folder of code alone.

means: A look back over a stretch of work by anyone - a person or a machine - saying what they saw, what they learned and what changes because of it; it touches what it is about and may answer another reflection.
not: retrospective (a ceremony at an iteration's end); post-mortem (only after failures); lessons learned (only what went wrong); review (already means code review)

means: The look around before acting: the question asked, what was found in plain words, and the sources it rests on.
not: A list of links.

means: The word first used on 2026-11-12 for what is now called the fulldome; with it went wall, which needs no replacement: a part of the whole is a lens.
not: see fulldome

means: Done by hand often enough (three times) or heavily enough (30 effort-minutes) that it asks for a tool.
not: Bad, or forbidden: a saturated action is simply the next candidate for automation.

means: A work someone made that a project stands on - a book, a paper, a page - with what is taken from it.
not: Research: a source is what was read, research is the reading and what came of it.

means: A place that produces: one idea or project keeping its own ocoeco data, gathering nothing. A git repository today.
not: project (only what has a repository and code); repository (a tool's word, and only where it lives today)

means: A concept's own text: what it is, in a sentence or two.
not: statement (the word two projects used for the same role, retired 2026-11-11)

means: The words a project speaks and exactly what they mean - and what they do not mean. ocoeco defines the shared words; a project adds its own.
not: Jargon: a vocabulary translates words into plain language.

means: Time spent on nothing while something else runs - a build, a reboot, CI - recorded by the tool that waits, with what was waited on.
not: Manual work: that is effort spent; waiting is effort not spent.

means: What actually happens: the backlog, the log, and what the gatherers record.
not: The plan of it.

means: How a project's steps are delivered and proven - its tools, checks, gatherers, tests and practices - each tied to the step it serves, with why we care. As in the workings of a clock.
not: A task to do: that is the backlog.
